correctness.rationale: From exact scalar sketched Galerkin and least-squares equations, orthogonalizing the two vectors v and Av yields independent Gaussian sketches. Rotational Gaussian invariance gives numerator projections Z/H with H² chi-square with ell degrees, proving reciprocal shifted Student for FOM and affine Student for GMRES. The shifted-Student density at zero is explicitly continuous and positive for d>0, yielding a 1/t absolute tail and divergent moments q≥1. Expanding the exact SPD energy error around the deterministic Galerkin minimizer gives infinite expected squared energy. The GMRES Student variance and true residual identity yield the claimed finite risk for ell>2 and the sharp moment cutoff. Finite checker replay independently guards the coefficients and algebra; infinite moment follows from proof, not sampling.

originality.rationale: The 2022 sketched-FOM/GMRES primary source defines both projection equations but reports stability phenomenology and embedding-conditional error estimates, not unconditional Gaussian coefficient laws. The 2023 randomized orthogonal-projection analysis similarly discusses occasional spikes. The 2024/2025 sketched Arnoldi analysis treats algebraic stability, not reciprocal-Student moment obstructions. Student and chi laws as such are standard; their precise insertion into FOM and GMRES, with infinite versus finite risk for the same SPD problem and every finite oversampling size, is the new implication. Four scientific database queries and focused primary-document comparisons found no claim-equivalent source; absence from an index is not proof of priority.
residual_risks: An earlier RGS preprint or other unindexed work may separately derive the same Gaussian inverse-Student moment law.

value.rationale: The initial Krylov step is a natural and consequential reduced projection in Krylov solves, and the defining papers document large random spikes but offer condition-on-embedding guarantees. Exact identification of a reciprocal pole proves that no finite amount of Gaussian oversampling can make the unconditional squared FOM risk finite, while the same sketch budget admits a finite second-moment GMRES residual and an exact moment threshold. This resolves whether typical accuracy and mean-risk certification can be interchanged and motivates explicit clipping, sketch rejection or risk-aware projection choices.
